newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Somali leader seeks wide participation in talks.
newsitem.headline: Somali leader seeks wide participation in talks.

text.p: Somali faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed left Ethiopia for Mogadishu on Wednesday in a bid to persuade rival leaders to attend reconciliation talks in November.

A spokesman for an alliance of 26 factions led by Ali Mahdi said he would meet south Mogadishu faction leader Hussein Aideed on Friday to try to convince him to attend the talks in Bosasso in northeast Somalia.
He said Ali Mahdi would then travel on to northwestern Somalia in an attempt to persuade Mohamed Egal, president of the self-declared republic of Somaliland, to attend the meeting.
Both Egal and Aideed boycotted talks in Ethiopia which led to the 26 factions forming a National Salvation Council before the Bosasso meeting to set up a provisional government for the country.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of its late dictator and president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
